introduction.text: Afghanistan is a landlocked country in Asia between Iran and Pakistan. Mountain ranges cover much of it, giving way to plains in the north and southwest.
Albania lies on the coast of southeastern Europe, just north of Greece. The Adriatic and Ionian seas meet its western shore, with mountains inland.
Algeria stretches from the Mediterranean coast of North Africa deep into the Sahara. The Atlas Mountains rise in the north, and another range, the Hoggar, rises from the southern desert.
Andorra is a small country high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain. Its towns sit in narrow valleys between mountain ridges.
Angola faces the Atlantic on the southwest coast of Africa. From the shore, the land rises steeply to a broad inland plateau.
Antigua and Barbuda is a Caribbean country built around two islands of the same names. The Atlantic lies to their east.
Argentina runs down the eastern side of the Andes in South America. Its landscapes include the grassy Pampas and the great plateau of Patagonia.
Armenia is a landlocked country in the Caucasus, where Europe and Asia meet. Mountain rivers flow down to the fertile valley of the Aras.
Australia occupies a continent between the Indian and Pacific oceans. Much of its interior is dry, while fertile plains stretch across parts of the southeast.
Austria is a landlocked country in central Europe, north of Italy. The Alps fill much of its west and south before giving way to gentler country in the east.
Azerbaijan sits on the western shore of the Caspian Sea, between Russia and Iran. Its capital, Baku, is on a peninsula that juts out into the water.
The Bahamas are a chain of low islands in the Atlantic, southeast of Florida and northeast of Cuba. Many of the islands are formed from coral limestone.
Bahrain is a group of low islands in the Persian Gulf, just east of Saudi Arabia. Much of the main island is a desert plain.
Bangladesh sits at the top of the Bay of Bengal in South Asia. Rivers have laid down much of its flat land, while hills rise in the southeast.
Barbados is a Caribbean island that sits out in the Atlantic, northeast of Venezuela. Its low coastal land rises gently toward hills in the centre.
Belarus is a landlocked country in eastern Europe, east of Poland. Much of the landscape is flat, with extensive marshland.
Belgium sits on the North Sea between France and the Netherlands. Flat land near the coast gives way to rolling hills and the wooded Ardennes in the southeast.
Belize is on the Caribbean side of Central America, south of Mexico and next to Guatemala. A low coastal plain rises into mountains in the south.
Benin reaches from a narrow stretch of Atlantic coast into the interior of West Africa. Togo is on one side and Nigeria on the other.
Bhutan sits high in the Himalayas between India and China. Fertile valleys break up the mountain ranges.
Bolivia is landlocked near the centre of South America. The Andes rise around a high plateau, while lower plains extend toward the Amazon basin.
Bosnia and Herzegovina is a mountainous country in southeastern Europe. It has a short stretch of coast on the Adriatic Sea.
Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa. Much of it is open, gently rolling land, with the Kalahari Desert stretching across the southwest.
Brazil stretches from the Amazon basin in northern South America to a long Atlantic coast. Its capital is Brasília, inland from the coast.
Brunei sits on the north coast of Borneo in Southeast Asia. It shares the island with Malaysia and Indonesia and faces the South China Sea.
Bulgaria is in southeastern Europe, with Romania to its north and the Black Sea to its east. Mountain ranges rise between stretches of lowland.
Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa, just north of Ghana. Its south has grassy savanna and a short rainy season.
Burundi is a small country in the hills of east-central Africa, between Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Lake Tanganyika runs along its southwest.
Cambodia lies in Southeast Asia between Thailand, Laos and Vietnam. Wide lowland plains open toward the Gulf of Thailand.
Cameroon sits on the Atlantic coast of central Africa, beside Nigeria. The land changes from low coastal plains to mountains in the west and open plains in the north.
Canada stretches across northern North America from the Pacific to the Atlantic. The Arctic Ocean borders it to the north, and mountains rise in the west.
Cape Verde is an island country in the Atlantic off the coast of West Africa. Volcanoes gave its islands their steep, rocky slopes.
The Central African Republic is a landlocked country near the middle of Africa. Most of it lies on a broad plateau north of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Chad is a landlocked country south of Libya. Northern Chad reaches into the Sahara, while open plains and lowlands stretch across the centre and south.
Chile is a long, narrow country on the Pacific coast of South America. The Andes rise along its eastern side, beside Argentina.
China stretches from high mountains and inland deserts across East Asia to the Pacific coast. Its eastern plains include broad river deltas.
Colombia sits at the northern end of South America, where the continent meets Panama. It has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean.
Comoros is a group of volcanic islands between Madagascar and the African mainland. The islands sit at the northern entrance to the Mozambique Channel.

The Republic of the Congo is a central African country with a short Atlantic coast. Its capital, Brazzaville, sits on the Congo River across from Kinshasa in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Costa Rica sits between Nicaragua and Panama in Central America. Volcanic mountains rise between its Caribbean and Pacific coasts.
Croatia curves along the Adriatic coast of southeastern Europe. Islands line its shore, while flatter plains stretch inland toward Hungary.
Cuba lies south of Florida, between the Atlantic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. Much of the island is open plain, with mountains rising in the southeast.
Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean, south of Türkiye. Mountain ranges rise on either side of its central plain.
Czechia is a landlocked country in central Europe between Germany, Poland, Slovakia and Austria. Bohemia lies in its west and Moravia in its east.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a large country in central Africa. A low basin fills much of its centre, and mountains rise along its eastern edge.
Denmark’s European mainland extends north from Germany, between the North Sea and the Baltic. Many of its towns also lie on islands, including Copenhagen on Zealand.
Djibouti is on the northeastern coast of Africa where the Red Sea meets the Gulf of Aden. Mountains separate its coastal plain from the inland plateau.
Dominica is a mountainous island in the eastern Caribbean. Its rugged interior was shaped by volcanoes.
The Dominican Republic occupies the eastern part of Hispaniola, a Caribbean island it shares with Haiti. Fertile valleys lie between its high mountain ranges.
Ecuador sits on the equator along South America’s Pacific coast. From west to east, the land changes from coastal plains to Andean highlands and then rainforest.
Egypt sits in northeastern Africa, with the Sinai Peninsula extending into Asia. The Nile runs through the desert and fans out into a delta before reaching the Mediterranean.
El Salvador faces the Pacific in Central America, between Guatemala and Honduras. A narrow strip of coastal land rises toward mountains in the interior.
Equatorial Guinea has a mainland region between Cameroon and Gabon on Africa’s west coast. Its territory also includes volcanic islands in the Atlantic.
Eritrea stretches along the Red Sea in eastern Africa, between Sudan and Djibouti. Its highlands descend eastward to a hot coastal plain.
Estonia sits on the Baltic Sea in northern Europe, north of Latvia. The Gulf of Finland separates its northern coast from Finland.
Eswatini is a small country in southern Africa between South Africa and Mozambique. Hills and mountains cover much of the country.
Ethiopia is a landlocked country in eastern Africa, west of Somalia. The Great Rift Valley cuts through its high mountain plateau.
Fiji is an island country in the South Pacific, north of New Zealand. Volcanoes formed many of its mountainous islands.
Finland is in northern Europe between Sweden and Russia. Its low hills are dotted with lakes, and its coast meets the Baltic Sea.
Mainland France stretches from the English Channel to the Mediterranean in western Europe. France also includes places overseas, such as French Guiana in South America.
Gabon sits on Africa’s Atlantic coast where the equator crosses the continent. Behind its narrow coastal plain are hills and stretches of savanna.
The Gambia follows the Gambia River through West Africa to the Atlantic Ocean. Senegal borders the country on its landward sides.
Georgia lies in the Caucasus between Europe and Asia. High mountains rise to the north and south, while its western lowlands open onto the Black Sea.
Germany is in central Europe. From north to south, its landscape runs from the Baltic and North Sea coasts to the Bavarian Alps.
Ghana is a West African country on the Gulf of Guinea, an arm of the Atlantic. Côte d’Ivoire lies to its west and Togo to its east.
Greece lies in southeastern Europe, where mountain ranges extend into the Mediterranean as peninsulas and chains of islands. Athens is its capital.
Grenada is an island country in the Caribbean north of Trinidad and Tobago. The main island has a mountainous centre formed by volcanoes.
Guatemala lies just south of Mexico in Central America. Mountain ranges separate its Pacific coast from the wide northern lowlands of Petén.
Guinea is on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, between Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone along the shore. The flat coastal land gives way to hills and mountains inland.
Guinea-Bissau is a West African country between Senegal and Guinea. Rivers cut deep into its Atlantic coastline, and the Bijagós Islands lie offshore.
Guyana faces the Atlantic on South America’s northern coast, between Venezuela and Suriname. Low coastal plains rise into rolling highlands inland.
Haiti occupies the western part of Hispaniola, a mountainous Caribbean island. The Dominican Republic shares the island to its east.
Honduras is a Central American country between Guatemala and Nicaragua. It has a long Caribbean coastline and a smaller opening to the Pacific at the Gulf of Fonseca.
Hungary is a landlocked country in central Europe. Broad plains cover much of the land, with hills and low mountains near the Slovak border.
Iceland is an island in the North Atlantic, northwest of the United Kingdom. Its interior has mountains and ice fields, and deep bays cut into its coast.
India extends from the Himalayas in the north to the Indian Ocean in the south. The Arabian Sea lies to its west and the Bay of Bengal to its east.
Indonesia is a chain of islands in Southeast Asia between the Indian and Pacific oceans. On many of the larger islands, mountains rise above the coastal lowlands.
Iran lies between the Caspian Sea to the north and the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman to the south. Mountains surround much of its dry interior.
Iraq is in the Middle East, west of Iran. Much of it is broad plain, with reed marshes in the south and mountains near the borders with Iran and Türkiye.
Ireland occupies most of an island west of Great Britain in the North Atlantic. Low plains fill the interior, while sea cliffs rise along the western shore.
Israel lies on the eastern Mediterranean coast, south of Lebanon. Its landscape includes coastal plains, central hills and the Negev Desert in the south.
Italy’s boot-shaped peninsula extends from southern Europe into the Mediterranean. Mountain ranges run through much of the mainland.
Côte d’Ivoire, also known as Ivory Coast, lies on West Africa’s Atlantic shore, west of Ghana. Most of its land is gently rolling plain, with mountains in the northwest.
Jamaica is an island in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba. Mountains cover most of the interior and give way to narrow coastal plains.
Japan is a chain of mountainous islands off the east coast of Asia. Tokyo, the capital, is on Honshu, the largest island.
Jordan is a Middle Eastern country northwest of Saudi Arabia. Along its western side, a deep valley holds the Jordan River and the Dead Sea.
Kazakhstan stretches across a broad sweep of Central Asia. Open grasslands called steppe give way to the Altai Mountains in the east and desert in the south.
Kenya sits on the Indian Ocean in East Africa, between Somalia and Tanzania. Moving inland, the lowlands rise to high country cut by the Great Rift Valley.
Kiribati is a Pacific island country spread across the equator. Most of its islands are low rings of coral called atolls.
Kuwait sits between Iraq and Saudi Arabia at the northern end of the Persian Gulf. The land inland from the coast is mostly flat desert.
Kyrgyzstan is a landlocked country in Central Asia, west of China. The high peaks of the Tian Shan surround a network of valleys and basins.
Laos is a landlocked country in Southeast Asia between Thailand and Vietnam. Most of its terrain is mountainous, broken up by plains and plateaus.
Latvia lies between Estonia and Lithuania on the Baltic Sea. Much of this northern European country is low, level land.
Lebanon sits on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean. The Bekaa Valley runs between two mountain ranges inland from its narrow coast.
Lesotho is a mountain country completely surrounded by South Africa. High plateaus and hills cover much of its land.
Liberia is on West Africa’s Atlantic coast between Sierra Leone and Côte d’Ivoire. Lowlands by the shore rise toward a plateau and mountains in the northeast.
Libya lies on North Africa’s Mediterranean coast, west of Egypt. Much of its land extends south into the Sahara.
Liechtenstein is a small country between Switzerland and Austria. The Rhine Valley runs along its western side, and the Alps rise in the east.
Lithuania is on the Baltic Sea in northern Europe, south of Latvia. Its low-lying countryside is scattered with small lakes.
Luxembourg is a small landlocked country between Belgium, France and Germany. Its rolling uplands slope toward the Moselle River in the southeast.
Madagascar is a large island off the east coast of Africa in the Indian Ocean. Mountains and a high plateau rise inland from the coastal plain.
Malawi is a long, narrow country in southeastern Africa. Much of its eastern side follows Lake Malawi, while hills and highlands rise inland.
Malaysia has two parts separated by the South China Sea. One extends along a peninsula south of Thailand, and the other occupies part of the island of Borneo.
The Maldives are a chain of low coral islands in the Indian Ocean, southwest of India. Many are grouped around lagoons in rings called atolls.
Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa. Its northern plains stretch into the Sahara, while southern Mali has grassy savanna.
Malta is a group of rocky Mediterranean islands south of Sicily. Cliffs line parts of the coast.
The Marshall Islands lie in the North Pacific, roughly halfway between Hawaii and Australia. Its two main chains are known as Ratak, or Sunrise, and Ralik, or Sunset.
Mauritania faces the Atlantic on the western edge of the Sahara. Much of its land is flat desert plain, with hills in the centre.
Mauritius is an island country in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar. On its main island, mountains rise around a central plateau.
Mexico lies in North America between the United States, Guatemala and Belize. Its long coasts reach the Pacific Ocean, the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea.
The Federated States of Micronesia is a Pacific island country between Hawaii and Southeast Asia. Its islands range from mountainous volcanic land to low coral atolls.
Moldova is a landlocked country in eastern Europe between Romania and Ukraine. Its gently rolling land slopes south toward the Black Sea.
Monaco is a small country on the Mediterranean coast of southern France, close to Italy. Buildings climb its rocky hills above the sea.
Mongolia lies between Russia and China. Its open grasslands stretch toward the Gobi Desert in the south and mountain ranges in the west.
Montenegro sits on the Adriatic coast of southeastern Europe. The narrow shore rises sharply into rocky mountains and high plateaus.
Morocco lies in the northwest corner of Africa, with the Atlantic Ocean on one side and the Mediterranean Sea on another. Inland, the Atlas Mountains rise above valleys and plains.
Mozambique stretches along Africa’s southeast coast, with Tanzania to the north and South Africa to the south. The Zambezi River crosses the country on its way to the Indian Ocean.
Myanmar is in Southeast Asia, between India and Thailand. The Irrawaddy River flows south through lowlands framed by mountains.
Namibia is on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa. The Namib Desert runs along the coast, and the Kalahari reaches into the country from the east.
Naoero is a small island in the Pacific Ocean, just south of the equator. A narrow ring of coastal land surrounds a higher, rocky interior.
Nepal is a South Asian country between India and China. Its landscape rises from southern river plains to the Himalayas in the north, where Mount Everest stands.
The Netherlands lies on Europe’s North Sea coast, between Germany and Belgium. Some of its flat land was reclaimed from water and lies below sea level.
New Zealand lies southeast of Australia in the South Pacific. Two large islands, the North Island and the South Island, make up most of the country.
Nicaragua lies between Honduras and Costa Rica in Central America. Its Caribbean side has broad coastal plains, while volcanoes rise near its Pacific shore.
Niger sits inland in West Africa. Sand dunes and desert cover much of the north, giving way to grasslands in the south.
Nigeria is on West Africa’s Atlantic coast, between Benin and Cameroon. The Niger River spreads into a delta as it reaches the Gulf of Guinea.
North Korea occupies the northern part of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia. Hills and mountains fill much of its interior, with deep valleys between them.
North Macedonia is a mountainous country just north of Greece in southeastern Europe. The Vardar River cuts across it, and several lakes straddle its borders.
Norway runs along the western side of Scandinavia in northern Europe. Deep, narrow inlets called fjords bring the Atlantic far inland between mountains.
Oman lies on the southeastern side of the Arabian Peninsula. Much of its interior is desert, and mountains rise near both ends of its long coast.
Pakistan is in South Asia, with India to the east and the Arabian Sea to the south. The Indus River crosses broad plains below the northern highlands.
Palau is a group of Pacific islands southeast of the Philippines. Its largest island is hilly, while many of the smaller islands sit low among coral reefs.
Palestine includes the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in western Asia. The West Bank lies inland near the Jordan River, while Gaza has a Mediterranean coast.

introduction.text: Panama sits on the narrow strip of land that joins Central and South America. The Panama Canal gives ships a passage between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Papua New Guinea lies north of Australia. It includes the mountainous eastern half of New Guinea, which it shares with Indonesia, and smaller islands in the Pacific.
Paraguay lies inland in South America between Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia. The Paraguay River separates wooded hills and grassland in the east from the low plains of the Chaco in the west.
Peru lies on South America’s Pacific coast. Travelling inland takes you from dry coastal plains across the Andes and down into Amazon rainforest.
The Philippines is a country of thousands of islands in Southeast Asia, east of Vietnam. Many of its islands have mountain ridges and coastal plains.
Poland lies in central Europe, east of Germany. Broad plains cover much of the country between the Baltic coast in the north and mountains in the south.
Portugal lies west of Spain on Europe’s Atlantic coast. Its territory also includes the Atlantic islands of Madeira and the Azores.
Qatar sits on a small peninsula jutting into the Persian Gulf from Saudi Arabia. Much of the land is flat desert.
Romania is in southeastern Europe, with a coast on the Black Sea. The Carpathian Mountains curve around the central region of Transylvania.
Russia extends from eastern Europe across northern Asia to the Pacific coast. Siberia, east of the Ural Mountains, includes enormous stretches of forest and tundra.
Rwanda lies inland in Africa, just east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its grassy hills rise toward mountains in the west.
Saint Kitts and Nevis is a Caribbean country made up of two neighboring islands. Both islands have steep volcanic peaks rising above the coast.
Saint Lucia is a mountainous island in the eastern Caribbean. Two pointed peaks, Gros Piton and Petit Piton, rise near the town of Soufrière.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a chain of islands in the eastern Caribbean. It includes the mountainous island of Saint Vincent and a string of smaller islands to its south.
Samoa lies in the South Pacific, roughly halfway between Hawaii and New Zealand. On its two main islands, Upolu and Savai‘i, narrow coastal plains give way to volcanic mountains.
San Marino is a small, independent country surrounded by Italy. Its hilly territory rises around Mount Titano.
Saudi Arabia occupies much of the Arabian Peninsula in western Asia. Sandy deserts stretch across its interior between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.
Senegal is on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. From the coast, low plains extend inland and rise into foothills in the southeast.
Serbia lies inland in southeastern Europe. Its northern plains give way to limestone hills and mountain ranges farther south.
The Seychelles are a group of islands in the Indian Ocean northeast of Madagascar. Some rise into rocky hills, while others are low coral islands.
Sierra Leone is on West Africa’s Atlantic coast, between Guinea and Liberia. Mangroves grow by the sea, and wooded hills lead toward mountains in the east.
Singapore is an island country in Southeast Asia, between Malaysia and Indonesia. Its main island and smaller islands sit beside busy shipping routes.
Slovakia lies in central Europe, south of Poland. The Tatra Mountains rise in the north, while the land opens into low plains to the south.
Slovenia lies between the Alps and the Adriatic Sea in Europe. Its short coastline is in the southwest, and mountains rise near the Italian and Austrian borders.
The Solomon Islands lie in the South Pacific, east of Papua New Guinea. Some islands rise into rugged mountains, while others are low rings of coral.
Somalia occupies the eastern tip of the Horn of Africa. Its coast follows the Gulf of Aden in the north and the Indian Ocean in the east.
South Africa sits at the southern tip of Africa. High ground fills much of the interior, and the neighboring country of Lesotho lies entirely inside South Africa’s borders.
South Korea occupies the southern part of the Korean Peninsula in East Asia. Much of the land is hilly, with broad coastal plains in the west and south.
South Sudan lies inland in Africa between Sudan and Uganda. The White Nile flows through a vast wetland called the Sudd.
Spain occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe. Its mainland has both Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts, with the Pyrenees along the border with France.
Sri Lanka is an island in the Indian Ocean, just south of India. Much of the coast is low and flat, but mountains rise in the south-central interior.
Sudan lies in northeastern Africa, south of Egypt, with a coast on the Red Sea. The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet at Khartoum and flow north as one river.
Suriname lies on the Atlantic coast of South America, between Guyana and French Guiana. Beyond its narrow coastal plain, tropical rainforest covers much of the interior.
Sweden lies between Norway and Finland in northern Europe. Mountains rise along its western side, and its long eastern coast faces the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Bothnia.
Switzerland lies inland in central Europe, north of Italy. The Alps rise in the south, and a belt of hills and lakes separates them from the Jura Mountains in the northwest.
Syria lies in western Asia, with a short shore on the Mediterranean Sea. Mountains separate the coastal plain from the drier plateaus inland.
São Tomé and Príncipe is an island country near the equator, off Africa’s Atlantic coast. Its two main islands are mountainous and were formed by volcanoes.
Tajikistan lies inland in Central Asia, west of China. The Pamir Mountains rise in its southeast, while rivers cut through valleys in the west.
Tanzania stretches along the Indian Ocean in East Africa, between Kenya and Mozambique. Inland, plains rise toward highlands and Mount Kilimanjaro.
Thailand lies in Southeast Asia, with coasts on the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand. Its landscape includes a broad central plain and a high plateau in the east.
Timor-Leste lies northwest of Australia in Southeast Asia. It includes the mountainous eastern half of Timor, a separate area on the island’s northwestern coast, and two smaller islands.
Togo is a narrow West African country between Ghana and Benin. Its Atlantic coast has lagoons, and its northern hills give way to open grassland.
Tonga is a group of islands in the South Pacific. Its western islands are volcanic, while many of its eastern islands are made of coral limestone.
Trinidad and Tobago lies off the northern coast of South America in the Caribbean. Trinidad and its smaller neighbor Tobago are the country’s two main islands.
Tunisia lies on North Africa’s Mediterranean coast between Algeria and Libya. Mountains rise in the north, while the southern plains meet the Sahara.
Turkmenistan is a Central Asian country on the eastern shore of the Caspian Sea. The Karakum Desert covers much of the country, with mountains near the border with Iran.
Tuvalu is a group of small coral islands in the South Pacific. The islands are so low and narrow that the ocean is never far away.
Türkiye links southeastern Europe and western Asia. The Bosporus, a narrow strait near Istanbul, separates the country’s European and Asian sides.
Uganda lies inland in East Africa, west of Kenya. The country has many lakes, including part of Lake Victoria along its southern edge.
Ukraine lies in eastern Europe with a coast on the Black Sea. Much of the country is open plain, with the Carpathian Mountains rising in the west.
The United Arab Emirates lies on the Arabian Peninsula between Saudi Arabia and Oman. Its coastal plains give way to sand dunes inland and mountains in the east.
The United Kingdom lies off Europe’s northwestern coast. It includes Great Britain, the northeastern part of Ireland, and many smaller islands.
The United States stretches across North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific. Alaska lies northwest of Canada, and Hawaii is a chain of islands in the Pacific.
Uruguay lies on South America’s Atlantic coast, between Argentina and Brazil. Gently rolling grasslands cover much of the country.
Uzbekistan is an inland country in Central Asia. Broad deserts and sand dunes give way to irrigated river valleys, including the Fergana Valley in the east.
Vanuatu is a chain of islands in the South Pacific. Many were formed by volcanoes, and narrow coastal plains sit below steep mountains.
Vatican City is an independent country entirely inside Rome, Italy. Its small territory sits on a low hill within the city.
Venezuela lies on South America’s northern coast, facing the Caribbean Sea. The Andes reach its northwest, with wide plains inland and highlands to the southeast.
Vietnam runs along the eastern coast of mainland Southeast Asia. Its long, narrow shape takes in northern mountains, central highlands and low river deltas.
Yemen sits at the southwestern end of the Arabian Peninsula, beside the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Steep mountains rise inland from a narrow coastal plain.
Zambia lies inland in southern Africa. The Zambezi River forms part of its border with Zimbabwe, where the water plunges over Victoria Falls.
Zimbabwe is an inland country in southern Africa, between Zambia and South Africa. The Zambezi River and Victoria Falls mark part of its northern border.
